items.stem: What does the custom connector questionnaire ask first about a source system?

options.text: How many engineers the partner can assign
Whether a native connector or the Glean Web Crawler already covers it
Which language the connector will use
Whether the statement of work is signed

items.stem: Which credential does the questionnaire prefer for content, permission, and activity data?

options.text: Read-only keys, where the source supports them
An administrator account with write access
A developer's personal token
Any key that never expires

items.stem: A source exposes only file names and dates, with no body text. What is the consequence?

options.text: Results will never appear in search
Glean will fetch the body from the viewURL
Ranking improves because documents are smaller
Results can be found, but Assistant cannot summarize them

items.stem: The source has no identity data that maps to corporate accounts. What is needed?

options.text: An allow-all ACL until identities are sorted out
Nothing; Glean resolves unknown users itself
A manual map of users to corporate identities
A people connector for employee records

items.stem: The source allows 600 requests per minute. What pacing does the SDK guidance suggest?

options.text: Exactly 10 requests per second to finish fastest
About 7 to 8 requests per second, leaving room for retries
As fast as possible, relying on 429 retries
One request per second, to be safe

items.stem: Which rate limit applies to the /indexdocuments endpoint?

options.text: 600 documents per minute
10 documents per second per IP
8,000 documents per minute
Unlimited for push connectors

items.stem: The customer's security policy requires the connector to run inside its own network. What is the documented choice?

options.text: Glean-hosted, because it keeps data inside the network
Either; hosting can be chosen after the build
Neither; custom connectors cannot run there
Self-host it; the network must allow pushes to Glean indexing endpoints

items.stem: Source users and SSO users share the same email addresses. How should the datasource reference users?

options.text: By the source's numeric user IDs only
By display name
By email, with isUserReferencedByEmail set to true
By group membership, with no users

items.stem: Why record how often permissions change in the source?

options.text: It determines the datasource category
It sets how often permissions and memberships must be refreshed
It decides whether activity is needed
It fixes the viewURL format

items.stem: The sandbox is 11 months old and misses newer permission patterns. How should this appear in scoping?

options.text: As a risk with a condition: refresh it before validation sign-off
As acceptable, because production gets tested later
As a reason to build against production
As irrelevant to permissions testing
